artworks.title: Pentheus Torn by Maenads (House of the Vettii, Pompeii)
artworks.description: Pompeii's House of the Vettii — Pentheus torn by maenads on the wall, Euripides' Bacchae in Roman domestic myth.

artworks.title: Death of Pentheus (Douris cup, Kimbell Art Museum)
artworks.description: Douris' cup — the Theban king ripped apart on Cithaeron, red-figure violence for the god he refused.

artworks.title: Death of Pentheus (Louvre G445)
artworks.description: Louvre G445 — Attic death of Pentheus, the spy in women's dress becoming the sacrifice the Bacchae demands.

artworks.title: Maenads Killing Pentheus (Meidias Painter, Kerameikos)
artworks.description: Meidias Painter circle — maenads killing Pentheus, late-classical vase fury for Dionysus' Theban revenge.

popCulture.title: The Bacchae
popCulture.creator: Euripides
popCulture.description: Euripides' tragedy is still the definitive stage of Pentheus' refusal — the king in women's dress, torn on Cithaeron.

popCulture.title: Pentheus
popCulture.description: The Theban ruler who spies on ecstasy remains the name for a city destroyed by the god it bans.
